item.title: Philippine armed forces back suspension of direct communication with China, raising risks of miscalculation, escalation: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14 22:02:00
Defense Secretary of the Philippines Gilbert Teodoro Jr. File photo: VCG The Philippine military has thrown its support behind Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr.'s suspension of direct military-to-military communication channels with China, as the Chinese Embassy in Manila warned that shutting down such contact fuels mistrust and narrows the space for crisis management amid continuing tensions in the South China Sea. The Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) claimed Tuesday that it "stands solidly behind and firmly supports" Teodoro's move, according to a report from the Philippine News Agency on Tuesday. A Chinese expert noted that the suspension of military-to-military communications between China and the Philippines would further undermine dialogue and mutual trust, while increasing the risk of misjudging each other's intentions. In the context of frequent maritime encounters, such miscalculations could severely weaken crisis management, raise the likelihood of sudden or unintended incidents, and expose frontline personnel on both sides to greater risks if tensions escalate unexpectedly because of less available communication channels. The AFP spokesperson, retired Rear Admiral Roy Vincent Trinidad, claimed communication mechanisms could only work when based on what he described as mutual trust, sincerity and support for international law. He claimed bilateral dialogue had failed because "the messages" did not match "the actions on sea, air and ground," and accused China of using direct communication as a "smokescreen," a report in the Philippine Star said on Wednesday. Trinidad also claimed that the AFP will continue to perform its sea patrol and "will keep performing rotation and resupply missions," according to the Philippine Star report. The Chinese Embassy in the Philippines, responding to the suspension, said "communication channels should remain open to avoid miscalculation and prevent tensions from escalating." The Embassy criticized Teodoro for shutting down military-to-military communication for "political self interests," warning that the move "fuels mistrust, narrows the space for crisis management, and pushes frontline personnel closer to confrontation," according to the Embassy's Facebook account. The current dispute indicates that the suspension did not begin this week. Coverage from Philippine-based media outlet the Daily Tribune said that Teodoro claimed on Tuesday that military-to-military communication with China had been suspended for nearly three years. In a May 2024 statement posted by the Philippine Department of National Defense, Teodoro said he had disallowed contact between the department and the Chinese Embassy since a courtesy call by then Chinese Ambassador Huang Xilian shortly after Teodoro took office in July 2023. Although China and the Philippines maintain other communication channels, they cannot fully replace direct military-to-military contact. Diplomatic channels are mainly used for broader policy and strategic coordination, while coast guard communication focuses more on specific maritime law enforcement. Military exchanges, by contrast, deal with more specialized and sensitive issues involving defense policy, military strategy and security concerns, Chen Xiangmiao, a research fellow at the National Institute for South China Sea Studies, told the Global Times on Wednesday. Chen noted that military communication serves as an important "backstop" for bilateral relations. Even when serious differences exist in the South China Sea, direct military contact can help clarify strategic intentions and security red lines, preventing specific maritime incidents from escalating into broader military confrontations. Given that the Philippine military also plays a role in planning and directing some maritime operations, restoring effective military-to-military communication remains important if Manila genuinely wants to manage disputes and reduce risks, Chen said. The latest military position comes as the Marcos administration stresses that the president intends to maintain engagement with Beijing. Palace communications undersecretary Claire Castro said that Manila would continue engaging with China, particularly in trade and investment, a report from News Watch Plus Philippines on Tuesday shows. Just days earlier, Marcos said his "greatest fear" was that a mistake by a seaman or soldier could develop into "something that goes out of control," while stressing the importance of managing problems and preventing misunderstandings in the South China Sea. The expert pointed out that the Philippine government's position appears to be internally inconsistent: while the presidential palace stresses dialogue and maintaining normal engagement with China, the defense establishment supports suspending direct military communication. Cutting such a channel would not make the Philippines safer, but would further weaken trust, increase the risk of miscalculation and ultimately impose greater security and political costs on Manila. Chen said this reflects a "double-track" approach: Manila portrays itself as willing to communicate and maintain overall bilateral stability, while continuing actions in the South China Sea that undermine existing understandings and create new friction. If the Philippines genuinely wants to manage risks, it should stop provocative actions, return to dialogue and restore effective crisis-management channels, including military-to-military communication.

item.title: First China-Pakistan army joint training features an all-Chinese equipment lineup, signaling deep interoperability: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14 21:19:00
Image of the opening ceremony of the China-Pakistan Karakoram 2026 joint army training held at a training base in Korla, Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Photo: Screenshot from the CCTV's military channel The first China-Pakistan army joint training Karakoram 2026 kicked off on Wednesday, with all weapons and equipment provided by the Chinese side, China Central Television's (CCTV) military channel reported. A military affairs expert said the choice of medium-weight wheeled vehicles for high-altitude operations, and Pakistan's use of an all-Chinese lineup, signal deepening military trust and potential future procurement. The opening ceremony for the China-Pakistan Karakoram 2026 joint army training was held at a training base in Korla, Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region. It is the first army joint training between the two countries, themed on joint counter-terrorism and clearance operations in high-altitude areas, said the report. The report said that all weapons and equipment in the training were provided by China, including Type 191 rifles, Type 201 squad machine guns, Type 11 armored assault vehicles, Type 08 infantry fighting vehicles, as well as artillery, unmanned and anti-unmanned systems. Wang Yunfei, a military affairs expert, told the Global Times on Wednesday that the two types of vehicles are both wheeled platforms. In high-altitude areas, wheeled armored vehicles have their own advantages. Unlike tracked vehicles, they are faster, especially during road maneuvers, and easier to maintain, making them well-suited for movement and combat missions on the plateau. The all-Chinese equipment lineup covers multiple categories and forms a relatively complete combat system, he said. On one hand, it shows China has provided weapons and equipment technology to Pakistan. On the other hand, these weapons could be procured by Pakistan in future military trade, further expanding the presence of Chinese equipment in the Pakistan Army. This joint training thus serves as a rehearsal and a process of familiarization. From a broader perspective, it also reflects strategic mutual trust, showing that military cooperation between the two countries has reached a high level. Building this kind of deep interoperability will lay a solid foundation for future joint operations between the two armies in counter-terrorism, border control and other areas, the expert said. Zhang Jueshe, another military affairs expert, told the Global Times that China and Pakistan complement each other well in the field of counter-terrorism, while cooperation can be advanced via intelligence sharing, joint operations, technology transfers, experience exchanges and economic cooperation. "China could provide Pakistan with technical and equipment support, including drones and smart combat platforms, to boost its surveillance and early warning capacity against terrorist groups, and also conduct experience training," he noted. Pakistan's experience in addressing complex border security situations, handling local separatist forces and coordinating counter-terrorism efforts can also provide references for China to tackle similar non-traditional security challenges, Zhang added. On Saturday, Senior Colonel Chen Xi, a spokesperson for the Chinese Ministry of National Defense, announced that in mid- and late October, Chinese and Pakistani armies will hold Karakoram 2026 joint army training in Korla, Xinjiang. Focusing on joint counter-terrorism operations in high-altitude areas, the activity will include skills training in UAV operation, on-the-move target search and firing, and long-range sniping, and cover joint command and live-force exercises. The exercise will expand the scope of China-Pakistan military cooperation, reflect growing mutual trust, and strengthen counter-terrorism collaboration through the sharing of experience and expertise, Zhang said.

item.title: Chinese PLA Navy sends Liaoning Carrier task group to waters of Western Pacific for training; Japan shouldn't hype legitimate activities: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-14 09:39:00
The Type 075 amphibious assault ship Anhui (hull number 33) conducts a joint exercise with the Liaoning carrier group. Photo: Screenshot from the CCTV News The Chinese PLA Navy on Wednesday sent the Liaoning Carrier task group to the waters of the Western Pacific to conduct training, which is organized in accordance with annual routine training plan, aiming to test and improve the group's realistic training level and continuously enhance the capabilities to execute missions. The move is in compliance with relevant international law and practices and not directed against any specific country or target, the PLA Navy said in a statement. On Wednesday evening, Japan’s Ministry of Defense claimed that it had spotted a total of four vessels, the Liaoning , two Type 055 large destroyers Anshan (Hull 103) and Wuxi (Hull 104), and Type 052D guided-missile destroyer Huainan (Hull 123), transiting southeast through the waters between Okinawa's main island and Miyako Island, heading toward the Pacific Ocean. Carrier-based fighter aircraft from the Liaoning were seen taking off and landing in waters approximately 250 km south of Ishigaki Island, Japan's Defense Ministry claimed in a statement. Zhang Junshe, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times that PLA warships, including aircraft carriers, regularly conduct far seas exercises in the Western Pacific, but Japan frequently hypes such activities. These far seas exercises conform to the international law and common practices, and the Japanese side should not hype such legitimate activities, Zhang said. Global Times

item.title: China-made L-15 jets on show in Marrakech, with recent appearances lifting trainer onto global stage: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13 21:25:00
Photo: VCG The United Arab Emirates Air Force's Al Fursan aerobatic team and Russia's aerobatic team Russian Knights will both perform as invited guests. It was announced on Tuesday in Beijing at a press conference for the 16th China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition, also known as Airshow China. This marks the second time since 2016 that two foreign military aerobatic teams will take part in Airshow China, performing the "ballet in the blue sky" alongside the PLA Air Force's August 1st aerobatic team, state broadcaster CCTV News reported. Earlier, in July, Chinese-built L-15E advanced trainer jets made their first appearance at a major US airshow as part of the UAE's national aerobatic display team, which attracted attention from international defense observers and earned high praise for their performance capabilities. China-made L-15 jets have been put on show in Marrakech, CGTN reported on Sunday evening. It is one of several recent high-profile appearances by the L-15 both in China and in the rest of the world. It showcases the aircraft's versatility and signals that Chinese trainer jets are winning broad recognition and trust from international users, a military affairs expert said. The UAE Air Force's Al Fursan aerobatic team showcased the advanced jet trainers on Saturday at Morocco's Marrakech Air Show 2026, which ran from Wednesday to Saturday, according to CGTN. Al Fursan, officially Fursan Al Emarat, is the UAE's national aerobatic display team. In 2025, the team marked a landmark transition, adopting the state-of-the-art Chinese-built L-15E - a fourth-generation fly-by-wire fighter trainer jet that the website of the US airshow says "defines the next chapter of Emirati aviation excellence." Described as a "fly-by-wire marvel," the Hongdu L-15E is capable of digitally processing every pilot input into aerodynamic perfection. In addition to the full-fly-by-wire digital control system, the aircraft also features key specifications such as a combined maximum thrust of 4,200 kilogram-force per engine, a maximum service ceiling of 16,000 meters, and a wingspan of 9.4 meters that is engineered for high-alpha maneuvers, said the website. The L-15 made its first Dubai Airshow appearance in November 2009, drawing wide attention at home and abroad, according to CCTV. Song Zhongping, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times that the UAE's acquisition and operation of the L-15E, and its display at multiple airshows, might help showcase the aircraft's capabilities and raise its global profile. It also shows Chinese trainer jets are winning broad recognition and trust from international users. The L-15 attracted interest from the UAE mainly because of its technical performance, as the Chinese aircraft is an advanced trainer jet that is second to none in the world, Wang Ya'nan, chief editor of Aerospace Knowledge magazine, previously told the Global Times. It can also carry weapons and serve as a light, multi-role combat aircraft, Wang said, noting that the plane is equipped with a full set of advanced electronic systems, and it comes with a wide range of munitions. All of the technologies and systems, including engines, can be directly supplied by China instead of from a third country, and the L-15 is also used by the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) under the designation of JL-10, Wang said. The JL-10 has also drawn attention recently. On July 30, the PLA Southern Theater Command (STC) and the China Coast Guard conducted patrols in the territorial sea and airspace of China's Huangyan Dao and its surrounding areas. The PLA has deployed new equipment such as the Navy's Type 054B frigate and the Air Force's JL-10 jet. From the footage released by the Chinese military, the JL-10 advanced trainer aircraft made its first appearance in a readiness patrol mission around Huangyan Dao, according to Song. Later, naval and air units of the PLA STC conducted readiness patrols in the territorial sea and airspace of Huangyan Dao and its surrounding areas on September 2, according to the STC's WeChat account. The JL-10 advanced trainer jet was seen multiple times in the footage carrying live missiles. Zhang Xuefeng, another Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times that based on the dialogue in the STC video, the JL-10 was flown by a flight instructor, likely either from a PLA academy or a flight training base. Having instructors participate in actual interception missions with combat units helps them gain real-world combat experience. This hands-on experience will allow them to better enhance trainees' combat awareness and training standards in future instruction.

item.title: 16th Airshow China to showcase Navy equipment on large scale, multiple Air Force combat platforms to appear for first time
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-13 14:38:00
A J-35A stealth fighter jet of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force flies over the Jinwan Airport in Zhuhai, South China's Guangdong Province, during the opening day of the Airshow China 2024 on November 12. Photo: Cui Meng/GT The Zhuhai city in South China's Guangdong Province is gearing up for the 16th China International Aviation and Aerospace Exhibition, also known as Airshow China, running from December 7 to 13. A press conference for the event was held in Beijing on Tuesday, briefing the public on the preparations and some highlights. The Global Times learned that, coinciding with the 30th anniversary of the airshow's launch, this year's edition will hit a new record in scale, expand international cooperation and extend its display dimensions. New equipment from both the Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Air Force and Navy will appear together, presenting the military's new-quality combat capability in a systematic way. Experts said Airshow China is a "national window" onto China's self-developed aerospace and defense technologies, and an important platform for technological exchange, trade talks and dialogue on peace, carrying significance for advancing the aerospace industry and maintaining regional peace and stability. Air Force to debut multiple main combat equipment As China's only State Council-approved international aerospace exhibition, Airshow China is held every two years. Since 1996, it has been held 15 times, growing from a regional show into one of the world's top five aerospace and defense events. Zhang Hu, a member of the Standing Committee of the CPC Guangdong Provincial Committee, executive vice governor of Guangdong Province and provincial government spokesperson, said this year's show will display over 3,000 pieces of equipment, with first-time exhibits estimated at 10 percent. The main exhibition area will host over 170 aircraft, with both domestic and foreign aerobatic teams performing. The PLA Air Force's exhibits have long been a highlight. In 2024, the J-35A stealth fighter jet's first official appearance made international headlines. "The star of Airshow China, which showcases Beijing's civil and military aerospace sector every two years in the southern city of Zhuhai, is the new J-35A stealth fighter jet," AFP said in its 2024 coverage, when the J-35A made its debut. Gao Xiang, deputy director of the political work department of the PLA Air Force, said this year's exhibits will cover reconnaissance, early warning, air defense, support, airborne operations, unmanned applications, intelligent equipment and munitions, fully presenting the service's equipment renewal and evolving combat system. "The lineup includes both combat-tested main combat platforms and publicly displayed upgraded equipment and new-quality combat capabilities," Gao said. "Some have made breakthroughs in type or quantity; others have innovated in air-ground coordination and display methods. The share of new-quality combat forces has increased, and multiple main combat equipment will make their Airshow China debut." The displays will show the public the Air Force's improved combat readiness and modernization achievements. Maritime display zone opens A key feature is the "one show, three zones" layout: the main venue at the Zhuhai International Airshow Center, the Gaolan Port maritime equipment display zone and the Lianzhou unmanned equipment exhibiting zone, extending the display of active-duty equipment to the sea and forming an integrated air, space, sea and land display system. "This year's airshow expands into the maritime dimension for the first time, opening the Gaolan maritime equipment display zone and enabling a large-scale, concentrated showing of active-duty Navy equipment," Zhang said. Zhang Junshe, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times on Tuesday that the expansion extends the display from "sky" to "sea," achieving comprehensive air, land, sea and space defense coverage and making the show more three-dimensional. In 2024, the PLA Navy brought real equipment to the airshow for the first time, including the J-15T carrier-based fighter, Z-9F carrier-based anti-submarine helicopter and Y-8 anti-submarine patrol aircraft. Two years later, the Navy is returning with a major maritime lineup. The Wall Street Journal noted the J-15T's appearance in 2024, reporting that China's navy showcased a new variant of its J-15 fighter that can be launched off aircraft carriers using a catapult system - a capability that Beijing has added to its newest carrier. "The Navy's move from a first appearance in 2024 to a large-scale display of active-duty equipment in 2026 marks a qualitative shift from 'testing the waters' to 'gaining a solid foothold,'" Zhang Junshe said. The expert added that Gaolan Port's deep-water conditions will allow the public to board ships for close-up visits, upgrading the experience from "looking at models behind a fence" to "immersive tours of real vessels." "Through this international airshow, the Navy will show its resolve to strengthen sea power and focus on combat readiness, raising public awareness and influence of its equipment." The Lianzhou unmanned equipment exhibition zone will serve as a demonstration platform for drones and anti-drone systems, according to the conference. Dynamic anti-drone demonstrations will be a highlight, with companies showcasing multiple countermeasures and the latest developments in drone counter-technology. Several new drone models will also take part in flight demonstrations. International platform As a major international aerospace and defense event, the airshow will again serve as a platform for global exchange and cooperation. This year's edition is more international than ever. Delegations from Russia, the US, France and Germany have expanded their participation, while companies from Belt and Road partner countries such as Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Singapore are deeply involved. More than 170 aircraft have registered for the main display area, a new record. Zhang Junshe said that since 1996, nearly 50 countries and regions and over 1,000 companies have viewed China's aerospace innovation and the systematic debut of new Air Force and Navy equipment through this window. Hao Changfeng, spokesperson for China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation, told the Global Times the company has participated in the event since 1996. "Over 30 years, our exhibits have grown from a few scattered items to a full spectrum of missiles, rockets, satellites, spacecraft and equipment, extending into commercial space, the low-altitude economy and space digital intelligence," he said. "Behind this shift is China's aerospace journey from catching up to running alongside, and in some areas leading." An anonymous military commentator who has attended the airshow multiple times told the Global Times on Tuesday that the event allows domestic and foreign companies to deepen exchanges and grasp the latest trends in global aerospace technology. Ahead of this year's show, Chinese aviation equipment has seen a string of delivery and procurement developments overseas. In August, Uzbekistan's state television publicly showed J-10CE fighters bearing the country's insignia, with six aircraft visible. Bangladesh is advancing procurement talks, with draft agreements prepared. "The J-10CE, as an advanced fighter independently developed by China, has won multiple overseas orders, entered service in other countries and achieved combat results. It has always been a focal point at the show. How the J-10 series, especially the J-10C, will be displayed this year will be closely watched," the commentator said.

item.title: Chinese pilots reveal more on China-Egypt drills: J-16, KJ-500 offsetting disadvantage of being outnumbered by Rafale, MiG-29
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-12 22:05:00
A Chinese J-16 fighter Photo: VCG Chinese state media aired a news program on Sunday featuring Chinese pilots who took part in the China-Egypt "Eagles of Civilization 2026" joint air training exercise from mid-August to early September, revealing fresh details from the drills featuring J-16 and Rafale fighter jets, including air combat tactics, refueling operations and candid exchanges between the two sides. An expert provided deeper insight into what the new details reveal. The exercise was not only an exchange of air force tactics between the two countries, but also an in-depth showcase of air force equipment development, reshaping perceptions of China's defense strength and defense industry in the Middle East, CCTV News reported on Sunday. An earlier report noted that on the first flight training day, Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) J-16s conducted air combat drills against Egyptian MiG-29 and Rafale fighters. A Chinese expert said this was the first joint exercise featuring both the J-16 and the Rafale, reflecting strong mutual trust and a high level of coordination between the two air forces. In the new CCTV footage, Wei Yuexin, a PLA Air Force pilot who served as tower command on the first day of training, said Egyptian fighters had displayed stronger close-combat maneuverability than their Chinese counterparts that day. Song Zhongping, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times on Monday that both the Rafale and MiG-29 are medium-weight fighters with relatively good agility, while the J-16 is a heavy fighter optimized for air-to-ground and air-to-sea strikes while retaining air combat capability. The Egyptian jets' advantage lies in close-range "dogfighting," roughly on par with China's J-10C. However, when it comes to beyond-visual-range combat, the J-16 should perform well, especially when guided by the KJ-500 early warning aircraft, Song said. This was one of the key lessons drawn from the training with the Egyptian Air Force, identifying each other's weaknesses, strengths and gaps, Song said. That lesson showed up later in the drills. CCTV reported that on the third day of training, the joint exercise escalated from single-aircraft and two-on-two engagements to a four-versus-six beyond-visual-range air combat scenario. China deployed four J-16s, while Egypt sent two Rafales and four MiG-29s. Facing this numerical disadvantage, China sent up a KJ-500 early warning aircraft for system-based operations. The KJ-500 can operate in complex electromagnetic environments, conducting surveillance, tracking and identification of conventional targets, and serves as a key airborne command hub. "When the air battle started, we forgot about the numerical disadvantage and forgot that they might be Rafales. We only remembered the timeline for missile evasion. We just needed to evade their weapons, and through tactical coordination, we made up for the numerical gap," Wei was quoted by CCTV as saying. He recalled that after that day's training, at 9:30 pm, Egyptian pilots were still looking for them, hoping to discuss the day's air combat. "What impressed me most was how much they appreciated and were interested in our use of electronic jamming. They thought our timing and jamming capability were excellent," Wei noted. Song commented that future air combat and system-based operations are not just about numbers, but about quality and systems. So while China may have only had four J-16s, it held a qualitative advantage. The KJ-500 acts as a "force multiplier," allowing the J-16, with its large weapons payload and long-range air-to-air missiles, to maximize its strengths and offsetting the numerical gap. The new CCTV video also showed more footage of a PLA Air Force YU-20A tanker refueling Egyptian Rafale fighters multiple times. On August 31, an official spokesperson for the Egyptian Armed Forces posted a photo on X showing the midair refueling, drawing widespread attention. A PLA YU-20A tanker refuels an Egyptian Rafale fighter. Photo: Screenshot from CCTV News "Egypt only has buddy refueling between MiG-29s, so they really valued this joint training opportunity," Wei was quoted by CCTV News as saying. The YU-20A's multiple refueling of Rafales and MiG-29s was extremely valuable experience for the Egyptian Air Force, Song said. As Wei noted, Egypt conduct buddy refueling between MiG-29s, which carries limited fuel and can leave the other MiG-29 with limited combat capability. The YU-20A, by contrast, can refuel any compatible fighters, with the core goal of giving other fighters greater range and endurance, which is critical. The performance of Egyptian Air Force pilots won praise from their Chinese counterparts. Wei said that while their refueling success rate and maneuvers may not have matched China's, "they improved very quickly, and by the end, their success rate had risen very fast." Egyptian pilots, in turn, spoke highly of their Chinese counterparts. One Chinese pilot said in the CCTV report, "When we chatted, they praised not only our skills but also our J-16 fighters and PL-15 missiles. I could feel it in their eyes. They were giving a thumbs-up to our country's development." The Chinese and Egyptian air forces held the Eagles of Civilization 2026 joint training exercise in Egypt from mid-August to early September. The training focused on subjects such as air combat tactics, air superiority operations and combat search and rescue, and included force employment drills, China's Defense Ministry spokesperson Senior Colonel Chen Xi said on August 14. As the second iteration of its kind, the exercise further enhanced mutual trust and traditional friendship, deepened substantive cooperation between the Chinese and Egyptian militaries, and contributed to regional peace and stability, Chen said.

item.title: China, Pakistan to hold first joint army training, leveraging 'complementarity' in counter-terrorism: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-11 21:19:00
Photo: VCG Chinese and Pakistani armies will hold Karakoram 2026 joint army training in Korla, Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, in mid and late October, a spokesperson for the Chinese Ministry of National Defense announced on Saturday. This will be the first joint army training conducted between the two countries, which will help the two sides deepen cooperation and strengthen interoperability in counter-terrorism, Senior Colonel Chen Xi, the ministry's spokesperson, said during a press conference on Saturday afternoon. A Chinese military affairs expert told the Global Times on Sunday that the exercise will expand the scope of China-Pakistan military cooperation beyond navy and air force drills, reflect growing mutual trust, and strengthen counter-terrorism collaboration through the sharing of experience and expertise. The two countries previously had held the Sea Guardians joint maritime exercises and the Shaheen joint air exercise. Zhang Jueshe, a military affairs expert, told the Global Times on Sunday that the significance of the first-ever joint army training lies in expanding military cooperation and deepening the China-Pakistan all-weather strategic cooperative partnership. "This marks an expansion of China-Pakistan military cooperation from specialized units in specific areas to regular army forces. It will deepen bilateral exchanges and reflect growing mutual military trust," Zhang noted. Jointly tackling cross-border terrorism will also aid to safeguard border security and the stability of both countries and contributes to regional peace, Zhang said, adding that deeper China-Pakistan counter-terrorism cooperation serves shared interests. China advocates joint efforts against terrorism in all forms, and this joint exercise embodies this position, he said. The China-Pakistan Sea Guardian IV joint naval exercise concluded on April 1 this year with the Chinese People's Liberation Army's (PLA) guided-missile frigate Daqing and Pakistani naval vessels parting ways in the northern Arabian Sea, according to a CCTV News report. The exercise kicked off on March 25 and was conducted in two phases: exchanges while at port and live sea drills. During the joint exercise, ships from both sides took turns serving as the command vessel, per the CCTV report. In 2023, the Shaheen-X joint air exercise, the 10th such bilateral air force training, was held in Jiuquan and Yinchuan, according to the Chinese Ministry of National Defense. The exercise at that time featured typical combat scenarios, including joint air defense, joint countermeasures and joint seizure-and-control missions to deepen practical military cooperation, enhance both sides' training standards and interoperability, and further advance exchanges and cooperation in military technology. "The Chinese military stands ready to work with Pakistan to explore new areas of exchanges, foster new highlights of cooperation, continuously enhance the capacity to respond to various security risks and challenges, and jointly safeguard regional peace and stability," a spokesperson for Ministry of National Defence said in 2023. For the upcoming training, focusing on joint counter-terrorism operations in high-altitude areas, it will include skills training in UAV operation, on-the-move target search and firing, and long-range sniping, and cover joint command and live-force exercises, according to the defense spokesperson on Saturday. Pakistan's counter-terrorism priorities cover five dimensions: intelligence early warning, military equipment, social governance, border management, legal and institutional building, Zhang said. Zhang said that China and Pakistan complement each other well in the field of counter-terrorism, while cooperation can be advanced via intelligence sharing, joint operations, technology transfers, experience exchanges and economic cooperation. "China could provide Pakistan with technical and equipment support, including drones and smart combat platforms, to boost its surveillance and early warning capacity against terrorist groups, and also conduct experience training," he noted. If the two sides strengthen cooperation in intelligence sharing and joint operations, China and Pakistan may end up establishing a joint intelligence analysis center to share terrorism-related intelligence, conduct joint law enforcement and precision strikes, and build an "comprehensive posture for countering terrorist organizations," he said. Pakistan's experience in addressing complex border security situations, handling local separatist forces and coordinating counter-terrorism efforts can also provide references for China to tackle similar non-traditional security challenges, Zhang added. Through comprehensive cooperation, the two countries can strengthen their counterterrorism capabilities and provide a solid foundation for regional peace and stability, Zhang concluded.

item.title: Exclusive video shows Philippine medical evacuation near Ren'ai Jiao conducted under China Coast Guard supervision
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-10 17:49:00
Exclusive video shows Philippine medical evacuation near Ren’ai Jiao conducted under China Coast Guard supervision By Feng Fan Published: Oct 10, 2026 05:49 PM A Philippine rigid inflatable boat from BRP Sierra Madre transfers an injured personnel to another rigid inflatable boat under China Coast Guard vessels' supervision on October 8, 2026. Exclusive footage obtained by the Global Times shows that a Philippine medical evacuation near China's Ren'ai Jiao on Thursday was carried out with China's permission and remained under China Coast Guard (CCG) supervision throughout the operation. The footage shows CCG vessel 5306 promptly warned the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) vessel 4409 to leave after the Philippine vessel entered waters near Ren'ai Jiao without China's permission. On humanitarian grounds, a rigid inflatable boat launched from PCG vessel 4409 was subsequently allowed to proceed to an area designated by the Chinese side, guided and monitored by a Chinese rigid inflatable boat. At the designated area, the Philippine rigid inflatable boat transferred an injured person from the BRP Sierra Madre, the Philippine ship illegally grounded at Ren'ai Jiao, with Chinese rigid inflatable boats and coast guard vessel supervising the operation, the footage shows. A PCG spokesperson claimed that CCG vessels had "obstructed" the evacuation mission, made dangerous maneuvers near a PCG vessel and used water cannons. China allows humanitarian medical evacuations, personnel rotations and resupply missions involving the Philippine ship illegally grounded at Ren'ai Jiao in China's Nansha Qundao, Chen Xiangmiao, a researcher at the National Institute for South China Sea Studies, told the Global Times. However, the Philippines has repeatedly used resupply missions to deliver construction materials to reinforce the ship's hull, seeking to use the vessel to illegally occupy the reef, Chen said. China therefore imposes controls on deliveries, and such resupply activities require its permission, he said. These resupply and personnel transfer operations have long been conducted under Chinese supervision and control, Chen said. Yet the Philippines sent a coast guard vessel for the medical evacuation without prior communication with China on Thursday, then portrayed itself as the victim to seek sympathy and challenge China's territorial integrity, he said. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning on Friday rejected Philippine claims that China had disrupted the medical evacuation, stressing that China would not waver in responding to any provocation and safeguarding territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests. At a regular press briefing, Mao said that a PCG vessel had intruded into waters adjacent to Ren'ai Jiao in Nansha Qundao of China without China's permission on Thursday morning. Mao said that following communication between the two sides, on humanitarian grounds, China gave timely permission to the Philippine side to evacuate the injured person by small boat and provided necessary assistance. Instead of acknowledging China's facilitation, individual Philippine officials have distorted facts and wrongfully accused China without showing the whole picture to the public, Mao said. This once again reveals their intention of provoking China and staging publicity stunts, which is rather despicable, she said. Mao's remarks followed a statement issued by the CCG on Thursday evening. CCG spokesperson Jiang Lue said that PCG vessel 4409 had traveled to waters near Ren'ai Jiao that day to evacuate an injured person from the Philippine warship illegally grounded there. Jiang added that, on humanitarian grounds, China had immediately allowed the injured person to be transferred by small boat. The CCG handled the matter in accordance with laws and regulations and provided necessary assistance, he said. Jiang said the Philippine side's remarks disregarded the facts, distorted the truth and sought to mislead the public. China has indisputable sovereignty over Nansha Qundao, including Ren'ai Jiao, and their adjacent waters, he said, warning the Philippine side to immediately stop its infringements, provocations and dissemination of false claims. item.title: Expert says K-8 trainer jet good fit for aviation academy's purpose, rebuts foreign media sensationalizing China-Laos support center
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08 21:18:00
JL-8 intermediate trainer jets, also known as K-8, perform a flight demonstration at the 2023 Changchun Air Show in Changchun, Northeast China's Jilin Province. Photo: VCG The China-Laos Joint Support and Training Center at Ban Keun Airport in Laos and the China-Laos Friendship Aviation Academy officially began operations on September 29. Their opening has drawn widespread attention and fear-mongering by some foreign media outlets. A military affairs expert said that the center makes use of K-8, a type of trainer aircraft that is fully consistent with the academy's purpose, and stressed that the center is meant to help Laos train intermediate pilots and build a modern air force, not to serve as a military base targeting any third party. The two institutions, jointly maintained and operated by China and Laos, aim to help Laos strengthen the training of its air force pilots. The establishment and operation of the two institutions reflect mutual respect and equal consultation between China and Laos, aligning with the domestic laws of both countries as well as international law and common practices, according to a statement made by China's Ministry of National Defense on September 29. The institutions are not directed against any third party and only aim to help further deepen practical cooperation between the two militaries and contribute to maintaining peace and stability in the region, a spokesperson for Ministry of National Defense said. However, some foreign media and social media accounts have speculated that the training base might expand its military use in the future. Reuters claimed on Tuesday, citing satellite images, that the images show what security analysts believe are eight K-8 "light attack jets" and more than two dozen support vehicles on a runway that is still being built. Experts cited by Reuters said that the planes appeared to be Hongdu JL-8 aircraft, another name for the K-8, which both the Chinese and Lao air forces operate. Laos currently has four of the planes, according to the annual assessment of the world's militaries issued by London-based International Institute for Strategic Studies. The JL-8 intermediate trainer jet is currently the main trainer aircraft used to train fighter pilots in China. It made its first flight on November 21, 1990, filling a gap in domestic general-purpose basic trainers. It has taken part in multiple National Day parades and major airshows, according to state broadcaster CCTV in August 2025. "It is a basic trainer, a single-engine jet basic trainer. The aircraft performs very well, and it has trained a large number of Chinese fighter pilots," Zhang Hong, chief designer and general manager of the Hongdu Aviation Industry Group under the state-owned Aviation Industry Corporation of China (AVIC), was quoted by the CCTV as saying. A JL-8 intermediate trainer jet, also known as K-8, is on static display at the 2025 aviation open-day activities of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Air Force and Changchun Air Show in Changchun, Northeast China's Jilin Province. Photo: VCG Song Zhongping, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times on Thursday that the JL-8 trainer is used by the PLA Air Force and by flight academies in countries including Pakistan. It is a transitional trainer mainly used to train intermediate pilots. The JL-8's presence at Ban Keun is telling. China wants to help Laos train intermediate pilots, because Laos' aviation capabilities are relatively weak. Moving from primary to intermediate pilot training shows that this base serves to teach, train and help Laos build a modern air force, Song said. Trainers came instead of fighter jets, and training should come first, Song said. This further highlights the purpose of the China-Laos Ban Keun training and support center: first and foremost, to help Laos build a modern air force. As construction continues, diplomats and analysts are keeping watch for any sign of air defense, ammunition and fuel storage as well as surveillance facilities - all of which could point to the base serving broader military functions beyond training, claimed Reuters. Regarding the sensationalization of the base and academy, Song said that if it were truly a Chinese overseas military base, it would have to target a specific direction and a specific country, so who is targeted? If the only target is non-traditional security threats, can it really be called a military base by conventional means? At most, China may use it as a support base to ensure flight safety, which falls under appropriate use. "If we truly treated it as an air base, we would have deployed a full system of combat capabilities there," Song noted. "But we are not targeting any neighboring country, they are all our traditional friends. There is no targeting at all," Song said. If there are any targets, they are non-traditional security threats such as terrorism and piracy, or for humanitarian rescue and disaster relief missions. These are not specific targets but broad ones, and they do not target any country or any third party - a core point. For this reason, the sensationalism has zero value, he added. Previously, Song said that Laos has a relatively small air force and has long lacked a systematic training system for pilots, maintenance crew and flight personnel. The center could systematically train pilots and ground support personnel, enabling independent talent cultivation rather than full reliance on overseas training, he said.
